questions.questionText: What are the two steps k-means alternates between until convergence?
options: Assign each point to its nearest centroid, then move each centroid to the mean of its assigned points
Sort points and pick the top k
questions.correctAnswer: Assign each point to its nearest centroid, then move each centroid to the mean of its assigned points
questions.explanation: This assign-then-update loop (Lloyd's algorithm) is the entire k-means procedure, repeated until assignments stop changing.

questions.questionText: Why does scikit-learn's KMeans commonly run with n_init > 1 (multiple random restarts)?
options: It's required for the math to work at all
Different random centroid initializations can converge to different (sometimes worse) results, so running multiple times and keeping the best avoids bad local convergence
It automatically picks the best k
questions.correctAnswer: Different random centroid initializations can converge to different (sometimes worse) results, so running multiple times and keeping the best avoids bad local convergence
questions.explanation: K-means is sensitive to its starting centroids; multiple restarts with different initializations, keeping the lowest-inertia result, reduces the chance of settling on a poor clustering.

questions.questionText: What kind of cluster shapes does k-means struggle with?
options: Non-convex shapes and clusters of very different densities (e.g. a ring around a center cluster)
questions.correctAnswer: Non-convex shapes and clusters of very different densities (e.g. a ring around a center cluster)
questions.explanation: Because k-means assigns points purely by distance to a centroid, it assumes roughly spherical, similarly-sized clusters — density-based methods like DBSCAN handle irregular shapes much better.
